text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you, the Spurs one. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah, yeah, all good. Alright? I'm Lewis.
A: Tracey. I recognised the shirt off your photo. My brother'd have words, he's Walsall through and through.
B: Walsall? Fair play, mate. Someone's gotta support 'em.
A: Oi! Cheeky. So what is it you do, Lewis?
B: I've got my own business, tiling. Bathrooms, kitchens, floors, all that. Out Bishop's Stortford way.
A: Oh, handy. Is that full-time then?
B: Erm, yeah, sort of. Depends on the week, you know. Some weeks it's mental, some weeks it's a bit quieter. I kind of pick and choose.
A: Must be nice, picking and choosing. I'd love that. I'm a fitness instructor at a leisure centre, but it's all sessional, so I take what they give me really.
B: Leisure centre? I play five-a-side at ours every Wednesday.
A: Course you do. Do you have a pint after?
B: Ha, how'd you know?
A: 'Cause that's every one of 'em at mine. They come off the pitch, straight in the bar. And then they wonder why their hamstrings go. Do you warm up?
B: Warm up? Erm. We sort of kick it about a bit first. That counts, yeah?
A: No, it doesn't! I'm telling you straight, you want to be doing proper stretches. Especially kneeling on floors all day. Do you wear knee pads?
B: Sometimes. When I remember. My knees are already starting to go, I'm not gonna lie. Thirty-four and I sound like a bag of crisps getting up off the floor.
A: Well, there you go. Wear the pads. And do some squats, proper ones, it builds the muscle round the knee. I get people in for inductions and I show 'em that first thing.
B: I do go the gym. In phases, like. I'll go every day for three weeks, then nothing for two months.
A: Ha, you and half of Walsall. January it's heaving, February it's me and the cleaner.
B: That's literally me. January I'm a machine.
A: Mm. So do you live round there then, Bishop's Stortford?
B: Yeah. I'm back at my mum and dad's at the minute, just while I save up, you know. Get a deposit together.
A: Oh, that's sensible. Nothing wrong with that. Does your mum feed you?
B: Every night, mate. Roast on a Sunday as well. Can't complain.
A: Lucky. I'm the one doing the feeding in our house, I've got a sixteen-year-old. I batch cook on a Sunday, chilli, spag bol, and it's gone by Wednesday. He'll have his tea and then he's back in the fridge an hour later.
B: Ha, sounds like me at sixteen. Sounds like me now, to be fair.
A: Your poor mum. Do you get away much, holidays and that?
B: Yeah, Marbella last summer with the lads. Did Benidorm for a stag an' all. You can't beat it really, flights from Stansted are like forty quid if you book early.
A: Benidorm! I went twice in my twenties. Never again though, I'm too old for it now. We go to the same caravan park in North Wales every year, near Towyn. My mum, my sister, the kids.
B: Wales? Does it not just rain?
A: Course it rains, that's half the fun. You sit in the caravan with a brew and play cards. Kieran pretends he hates it but he's down the arcades every night.
B: Fair enough. I dunno, I'd want a pool bar, me.
A: You'd be stood in the rain with a pint by the end of the week, I'll bet you—
